newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH HOUSE ALLLOWS FOR NUCLEAR ARMS DEPLOYMENT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH HOUSE ALLLOWS FOR NUCLEAR ARMS DEPLOYMENT.

text.p: The lower house of Czech parliament on Friday approved a law on nucelar materials which could eventually allow the stationing of NATO weapons on Czech territory.

The law, which still requires finall approval in the new upper chamber the Senate, sets up rules for the development, import, production, transfer, ownership, storage and other activities connected with nuclear materials.

The law is aimed mostly at rules on nuclear power use, but in consideration of potential requirements for NATO membership, the parliament dropped a clause which would have banned nuclear weapons to be stationed on Czech territory.
It effect it permits deployment if agreed in an international treaty.

The country is widely considered as one of the leading former Soviet satellites to join the western security alliance along with Poland and Hungary, but NATO has yet to say when or with whom it would expand its membership.
A decision on the who and when is expected to come from a summit of NATO leaders in Madrid next July.
NATO has not yet said if new members would be required to host nuclear weapons, as is required of current members.

The Unites States recently said it would not want new members to deploy NATO nuclear weapons as a condition for membership, a move interpreted as a concession to Russia which is bitterly opposed to the alliance's expansion.
Opinion polls show Czechs split on the need for the country's membership in NATO, but a solid majority are opposed to deploying nuclear weapons, after living with them for years as Soviet surrogates.
The Soviets removed their troops and their weapons earlier this decade, after Prague's 1989 revolution over communism.

The Czech law passed on Friday also defines rules for the commercial use of nuclear power, in connection with the new Temelin nuclear power station under construction in the southern part of the country close to the border with Austria.
The Czech Republic has one operating nuclear power plant at Dukovany in the southeast part of the country.
